input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
Keep a dictation alive when the next recording starts

Pressing the trigger again while the previous dictation was still in whisper
lost it whole. Two causes, both in the start-of-recording path:

  * tryWarmup() called pipelineReset(), wiping `results` and putting
    `finalizing` back to false — segments that came back afterwards were
    written into the new dictation's state and never assembled.
  * it also rm -rf'd the one shared chunks/ directory, deleting audio the
    previous dictation's ffmpeg was still concatenating.

A 92-second dictation vanished behind exactly two log lines: "pipeline: seg 2
concat FAILED (code=254)" and "seg 2 complete (done=1/?)".

Pipeline state is now per dictation. pipeNewJob() mints a job per keypress
with its own generation, chunk directory (chunks/g<N>), segment files and
results; pipeStartJob() detaches the previous job instead of resetting it, so
it keeps transcribing and delivers its own text. Nothing in flight reads
`pipe` any more — dispatchSegment captures its job, onPipelineDone and
pipelineFinalize take it as an argument — and the overlay and progress bar
stay with the current job only.

A detached job's transcript is queued rather than typed: it lands while the
user is still holding fn+ctrl, and both output modes post keystrokes. The next
insertion prepends it, so both dictations arrive in the order they were
spoken; every path that produces no text of its own flushes the queue instead
of stranding it. Emergency stop abandons every live job and rescues an
already-finished transcript to the clipboard.

Audio is deleted only by the job that owns it (pipeCleanup), and the shared
parent directory only at load.

11 new checks cover the class: a job finishing behind a newer recording keeps
its text, is not typed into the recording in progress, does not move its
progress bar, arrives with the next insertion oldest-first, and is dropped
after an emergency stop; plus the structural guards on tryWarmup, startRecording
and dispatchSegment. 103 checks pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
